neutral_facts.value: The accused was the last person seen with the victim, a female child aged about 6 years. The victim was last seen with the accused at her residence. A child witness reported seeing the accused and the victim together. The accused led the authorities to the victim's body, which was found covered with stones and branches. The victim sustained severe head and ear injuries, and the post-mortem report indicated the injuries were antemortem. Bloodstains on the accused's shirt matched the victim's blood group. The accused had a motive for murder due to a dispute over wages. The accused made an extra-judicial confession admitting to the crime. The accused's shirt was recovered at his instance, and no injuries were found on his body, ruling out self-inflicted bloodstains. The accused was found to have led the authorities to the victim's body, which was covered with stones and branches.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased was last seen with the accused, there was an extra-judicial confession from the accused, blood-stained shirt of the accused was recovered, the dead body was found at the instance of the accused, and there was motive for murder.

quotes.text: The deceased was last seen with the accused; extra-judual confession of accused; recovery of blood-stained shirt of the accused and the dead body at the instance of the accused and motive for murder.

defence_argument.value: The accused contended that there were doubts as to whether the death was homicidal and that the blood group of the accused was not tested to ascertain whether the blood stain on his shirt could be of his own blood.

quotes.text: In appeal to this Court the appellant-accused inter alia contended that there were doubts as to whether the death was homicidal.

The High Court noted that when at the instance of the appellant, his shirt was recovered and when the appellant was physically examined, it was found that there were absolutely no injuries on the body of the appellant.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the chain of circumstances against the accused was complete and that the death was homicidal based on the evidence of the post-mortem report.

quotes.text: In view of the specific statement of PW-6 (the doctor, who had conducted the post-mortem) who ruled out the possibility of the deceased having fallen down, either on her own or by way of an accidental fall by which she could have sustained the injuries, the conclusion that the death of the deceased was a homicidal one, has become an irreversible one.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed due to the overwhelming evidence proving all the circumstances against the accused, including the homicidal nature of the death, the last seen theory, the blood-stained shirt, the recovery of the body, and the motive for murder.

quotes.text: In view of the overwhelming evidence available on record, which proved every one of the circumstances put against the appellant and which has been examined in detail by the trial Court as well as by the High Court, there is no merit in the appeal.
